title: Neural memory: early optimism, failed retrieval role, parked integration

historical_claims.statement: Adding neural affinity to Engram retrieval improves memory recall without materially degrading existing recall behavior.

evidence.statement: Two clean evaluation runs found catastrophic direct-recall loss at every tested neural affinity weight; re-ranking was disabled.
The generation-mode evaluation produced a clean null: hints were emitted, but no metric improved beyond noise.
The 64-dimensional value configuration was numerically unstable and was reverted to 32 with fail-closed guards.
The neural layer is parked and default-off; it cannot improve retrieval as integrated, and reactivation requires a concrete need plus a new predeclared gate.

evidence.scope: possible future use of the existing surprise signal
evidence.statement: The label-free surprise signal may be better suited to novelty or anomaly use, but that reframe has not earned product status.
